newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Mixed trading seen in UK tobacco stocks.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Mixed trading seen in UK tobacco stocks.

text.p: The UK stock options market was a hive of activity on Wednesday as the London stock market staged a brief comeback after three days of losses, dealers said.

There was mixed trading in options of tobacco companies. The main deals in Imperial Tobacco IMT.l were from traders selling long dated put options possibly as a means of acquiring the shares if the stock price falls below the strike price. That is when the puts will be assigned.
If the stock price fails to fall, the options seller will receive the put premium as compensation. One trader sold 1,600 February 360 puts in Imperial Tobacco at 16p.

In a another deal, 700 February 390 puts were sold at 32p which was in contrast to the main deal in B.A.T Industries where 500 October 500 puts were bought for 41p which will make money if B.A.T shares fall.
At the close of business on the stock market, shares in Imperial Tobacco had slipped a penny to 370-1/2p while those of B.A.T were down 13p to 535-1/2p.

Over in British Telecommunications a put spread was the biggest trade and this involved selling 1,000 August 460 puts at 8p as well as buying 1,000 August 500 puts at 33p for a net debit of 25p. Maximum profit at expiry will be 15p if the shares fall below 460p.
BT shares gained a penny to 484-1/2p.

The biggest trade in mining group Rio Tinto was from a buyer of 1,000 February 1050 puts at 78p and in banking group Woolwich -- which made its stock market debut on Monday -- 400 July 300 puts were sold at 9p.
Some attention was also directed to the retail sector -- following pleasing results from Dixons Group -- where, in Kingfisher, there was a buyer of 500 August 700 calls at 23p.
Kingfisher shares jumped up 27p to 691-1/2p while Rio Tinto fell 2-1/2p to 1006-1/2p and Woolwich fell 6-1/2p to 294-1/2p.
